messages.subject: Re: density estimate from multiple- point transects
parts:
Dear William, list,

From your text below it was not clear (or I missed it!) what you have=20
defined within Distance to be the strata. By using the "resample=20
samples" ("within strata") option, and if each transect is essentially a=20
strata with 11 points each (and only valid if it is ok to treat these as=20
11 independent samples - ultimately depends on your design), I guess=20
what you are doing might be OK (although 11 independent units for=20
resampling might be at the low end). But you might have defined things=20
differently, so hard to say for sure.

Re your mention of the use of MCDS, more than using transect (which=20
might be a proxi for some variables that do change at a transect scale)=20
I would tend to use whatever variables you might have which actually=20
have a direct impact on detectability, like habitat, observer, group=20
size or time of day, to mention a few examples. Transect per se would be=20
a rather weird variable to use in MCDS, as I can't see how that, per se,=20
would have an impact on detectability.

Cheers

Tiago

Note: in general I find it potentially misleading/dangerous to estimate=20
density at a point level, but I guess it might depend on the specifics=20
of your study.


On 22/11/2012 04:15, William Marthy wrote:
> > Hello....
> >
> > I am starting to use distance sampling to analyze my bird data...I
> > collected bird data using point transect method, and I had 11
> > transects (each transect was 2 km length) and within each transect
> > there were 11 point counts (each point was 200 m apart). Beside that,
> > these 11 transects were at least 1 km apart....and I selected these
> > transects to represent degree of forest degradation in the study
> > area.
> >
> > Each transect was surveyed three times (also means that each point
> > was visited three times - survey effort per point was 3).
> >
> > Now I tried to the bird density estimate for global (the whole
> > transect), specific transects, and points. I already know how to
> > import the data and do the analysis but I am not sure whether my
> > approach is correct due to the sampling method that I used (multiple
> > transects but separated at least 1 km).
> >
> > I have read the manual, and the intro to distance sampling..and also
> > browse this mailserve but still could not find the answer...
> >
> > Nevertheless...in this case I have tried the following approach:
> >
> > 1. Using CDS engine and use bootstrap variance estimate (I select
> > non-parametric bootstrap with level of resampling "resample samples".
> > It was certainly took sometime but I think it was ok and produced
> > quite a nice result. The number of samples: 256
> >
> > I then went further to check the density estimate per-transect
> > (stratified but with pool detection probability) which also still
> > provide a good result..
> >
> > Question: 1. based on my sampling design, is this a correct approach
> > or is there any other way to deal with this type of data? 2. I have
> > read about MCDS..and think that this might be better approach where I
> > will treat the transect as covariate (but have not tried yet)...and
> > without have to use the bootstrap option
> >
> >
> > thank you for the time
> >
> > William
